entries.original: The morning read. Every half hour the system goes back over your workspace on its own and writes down what it noticed, in plain sentences. You get the short version and the one thing worth doing first.
entries.replacement: Morning briefing. Every 30 minutes, Antaeus reviews workspace data for changes and risks, then summarizes those findings in plain language. Each morning, it ranks the highest-priority action and shows the reason for that ranking.
entries.rationale: Near-twin of unit 95 (same claim, shorter). Reuses the approved wording ("Every 30 minutes, Antaeus reviews", "those findings in plain language", "ranks the highest-priority action"); drops the three examples the scene itself shows. "Then" replaces a second "and" so the sentence parses on first read, and "the reason for that ranking" avoids the draft's "the reason that action ranks first", where "that" can be misread as a conjunction. Removes the personification ("noticed", "on its own") and "the one thing worth doing first". Render note for all four captions, measured with the page fonts loaded: each is one line taller on desktop (92→116px); at 390px three are one line taller and the handoff caption two (188–212→212–236px); at 360px one to two lines taller (188–212→236–260px). Nothing clips and there are no page errors.

entries.original: A live call. Discovery Studio is a console you run the call from, not notes you write after it. It shows the question, what to listen for, and the moment they answer you tap what you heard — it hands you the exact next line.
entries.replacement: Live discovery call. Discovery Studio is the console you use during the call, not a place for notes afterward. It shows the current question and what to listen for. Select the buyer response you heard, and Antaeus shows the recommended follow-up question.
entries.rationale: Near-twin of unit 144 (the Discovery tab caption). Defines Discovery Studio literally on first use (COPY_STANDARD §4), reuses the approved "Select the buyer response you heard … recommended follow-up" wording, and drops "hands you the exact next line" (personification + "line"). Avoids bare "evidence" from unit 144 per canon §13. "During the call" (the bold label directly before it names the call) replaces the draft's "during a discovery call", which repeated "discovery" and made this the tallest caption at 360px (284px; now 260px).

"Going quiet" is the idiom COPY_STANDARD §13 replaces. The scene is a projected deal loss; the map already uses "deals at risk" for this concept (unit 39, leaf "3 deals are at risk").

entries.original: A deal going quiet. Future Autopsy writes the story of how a deal dies before it does — names the pattern, counts the days you have left, and routes you to the room where the fix happens.
entries.replacement: Deal at risk. Future Autopsy projects deal-loss risk. For an open deal, it shows how the deal is likely to be lost, the recurring risk pattern, and the estimated days until that loss, then links to the workflow where you can address the risk.
entries.rationale: Near-twin of unit 167. COPY_STANDARD §4 keeps the name Future Autopsy only if the copy says it projects deal-loss risk, so the first sentence does that. "Counts the days you have left" becomes "the estimated days until that loss" (unit 198's "estimated time remaining", with the end point named; "that loss" refers to "how the deal is likely to be lost" in the same sentence). "Routes you to the room where the fix happens" → "links to the workflow where you can address" (unit 167).

entries.original: Warby Parker dies in 20 days, and here is how.
entries.replacement: Warby Parker is projected to be lost within 20 days.
entries.rationale: Near-twin of units 166/200 ("Warby Parker dies in 20 days."); uses their approved replacement verbatim. The extra clause "and here is how" is dropped because the paragraph directly below gives the projected sequence, and the shorter headline matches the two static scenes.

entries.original: You have one champion and no one above him. Marcus goes quiet in week two, nobody signs, and it closes as no decision — the way most of your losses have gone.
entries.replacement: The deal has one champion, Marcus, and no one senior to him is involved. Antaeus projects that Marcus stops responding in week two, no one signs, and the deal closes as no decision, like most of your lost deals.
entries.rationale: No static twin. Follows evidence → projection → comparison (COPY_STANDARD §7): the evidence (one champion, no one senior to him), then what Antaeus projects, then how most past losses ended. Keeps the projection explicit ("Antaeus projects that …") rather than a hypothetical "If …", and fixes the draft's "no one else signs", which implied Marcus could sign. Replaces "goes quiet" with the observable behavior and "it" with "the deal". Keeps Marcus, week two, and "no decision". Measured with page fonts: two lines on desktop like the original (the draft needed three), one line more than the original at 390px and two more at 360px, the same height as the draft at those widths.

"The smallest fix" is already plain English; dropping "The" makes it a noun label (COPY_STANDARD §14) and gives the action more room in this single-line, ellipsis-truncated row. "Smallest corrective action" (the map's prose wording, unit 198) would leave only 130px at 390px, so it is not used in this row.

entries.original: The handoff. Seven parts a first hire reads on day one, written as prose rather than a dashboard — and each one carries a thing to notice that no single room could have told you on its own.
entries.replacement: Sales handoff. The handoff is an operating guide that a new hire reads on day one. It covers seven readiness areas in prose rather than in a dashboard, and each area includes one pattern that Antaeus finds only by comparing data across different workflows.
entries.rationale: No static twin for this sentence. Written as complete sentences like the other three captions; the draft's first sentence had no main verb (COPY_STANDARD §19). Uses the map's terms: "operating guide" (unit 56), "new hire … day one" (unit 55), "readiness areas" (unit 75, which renamed "parts"). "A thing to notice that no single room could have told you" becomes a literal description of the cross-workflow pattern, which the map renders as "Pattern: …" (unit 78). "Workflows" instead of "product areas" avoids two meanings of "area" in one sentence.
